title: Co-Training Generalized Segmentation Networks with Real and Synthetic Data
content: Here we demonstrate synergy between real and synthetic data in training generalized segmentation networks for cryo-ET data. To do this we used “synthetic cytoplasm” derived from CryoTomoSim with varied simulation parameters and a small amount of hand-segmented real cellular data to train an initial model, which was used to segment a set of tomograms from a variety of cell types. Subtomograms and their segmentations from trouble regions were then extracted and hand-corrected before being added to the original training set, and a new iteration of the model was trained. This process was repeated until the full set of tomograms could be segmented by the same network. The result is NeuralSeg, a generalized cryo-ET segmentation network capable of segmenting a subset of macromolecules (actin, cofilactin, microtubules, ribosomes, TriC) and membranes within tomograms derived from all domains of cellular life. By leveraging CTS outputs, which provides a perfect ground truth, this co-training approach avoids laborious de novo hand annotations of training data and allows one to focus only on the regions of the tomogram where the network underperformed.
